text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Gemma.
B: Joanne. I'm in Frome.
A: Sutton-in-Ashfield. Notts.
B: Right. What do you do?
A: Builders' merchants. I manage it. You?
B: Senior carer. Dementia home.
A: That's hard work.
B: It is. Yours too, I'd imagine. My partner's a joiner, he's always in and out of a builders' merchants. Moaning about the prices.
A: They all moan about the prices. Then they ask for a trade discount on top of their trade discount.
B: That sounds like Mark.
A: Is he self-employed?
B: Yes. Van's always parked across half the street. The neighbours love us.
A: Lee's an electrician. Same thing, tools in the hall instead.
B: Erm. I'll be honest, I looked at your photo and thought you looked tired. Sorry. I don't mean that rudely. I just recognised it.
A: No, I was. Stocktake week. I'm always knackered after stocktake.
B: Is it a big team?
A: Nine. Which is never enough. I got the job 'cause I knew the stock. Nobody told me it'd be mostly people. I'm not great at the people bit, if I'm honest.
B: I think people who say that are usually better at it than they think. The ones who think they're brilliant at people are the ones I worry about.
A: Maybe. My assistant, Dawn, she does the nice bit. I do the telling-off bit.
B: I'm the telling-off bit at mine. I won't sign off notes I haven't checked. Makes me very popular.
A: Same with stock counts. Regional manager wanted me to round something up once. I didn't.
B: Good. Do you get time off, or is it just work and sleep?
A: Dog, mostly. Mabel. Staffie, she's old. Round the reservoir every night. And I'm doing a lot with my dad at the minute. He had a stroke last year.
B: Oh. I'm sorry. How's he doing?
A: Alright. Better than he was. Speech came back mostly. He gets frustrated. Mum gets frustrated with him getting frustrated.
B: That's very normal. It's often harder on the person living with them. My mum's starting with memory things, so, erm. I know a bit about watching that from the other side, now.
A: That must be worse, doing it for a job.
B: Sometimes. You know too much about what comes next. I've got a greyhound, Pip, she's the one who keeps me sane. Long walks before shifts.
A: Dogs are better than people.
B: Most days, yes. Do you—
